questions.question: The ledger's request has an 8192 budget with 2048 reserved for max_tokens. How much is left for the input side?
options: 7248 — the sum of the five ledger entries
944 — the room left in the window
8192 — the input side is unaffected by the reserve
questions.explanation: See the "One contract, shared by input and output" section: the ledger's request reserves 2048 for max_tokens, leaving 6144 for input.

questions.question: Of the three ways window overflow ends, which is the most dangerous?
options: Truncation — the input is chopped head or tail and the model sees a mangled text
Silently dropped history — the application trims old turns before sending, so the request succeeds and the answer flows while the model never knows it lost context
An error — the API rejects the request with a 400-class status
The output gets squeezed out, generation stops mid-sentence, and finish_reason is marked length
questions.explanation: See the "Three ways overflow ends" section: the third, silently dropped history, is the most dangerous — the first two are at least visible, while this is a quiet failure where the logs all look fine.

questions.question: In context engineering, which trade always goes last?
options: Compressing distant history into a summary
Keeping only the most relevant retrieved passages instead of whole documents
questions.explanation: See the "Context engineering: what to pack into a finite budget" section: only last, trim the system prompt — that one always goes last, because role and boundaries are the safety floor.
